summary: Phase 149O.1H.4 -- HATP Timestamp Canonicalization Final Independent Re-Verification: verification-only phase, independently re-verifying the 149O.1H.3 repair of B-149O.1H-1 across the entire relevant HATP Wave-3 timestamp/constructor/canonicalization semantic domain. Independently reconstructed the exact production diff (01bacf8a..acb511bb): exactly one file changed, src/pcae/core/human_approval_trusted_provenance.py, UNRELATED = 0. Independently loaded the pre-repair source at commit 01bacf8a via importlib (isolated module name, never touching sys.modules for the live production import) and reconfirmed the historical defect is real: .0000001Z and .0000009Z both ACCEPTED, both canonicalize to 2026-01-01T12:00:00.000Z, both produce canonical payloads with the identical issued_at bytes. Independently reconfirmed the current interpreter (Python 3.14.5) still truncates datetime.fromisoformat for 7+ fractional digits. Independently inspected the current guard (_FRACTIONAL_SECONDS_RE, _reject_excess_fractional_precision, called from _parse_iso_timestamp) via source-position comparison (inspect.getsource) and confirmed the guard call textually and behaviorally precedes the datetime.fromisoformat call: RAW PRECISION VALIDATION PRECEDES LOSSY ISO DATETIME CONVERSION, for every input shape the guard's regex actually matches. Independently re-tested the full fraction-length matrix (0..12 digits), the seven-plus-digit adversarial matrix (.0000001/.0000009, .0010001/.0010009, .1234561/.1234569, .9999991/.9999999, .123456789/.123456780, .000000000001/.000000000009) across Z/+00:00/+01:00/-05:00 suffixes, the millisecond-domain separation (000000/001000/123000/999000 accepted; 000001/000999/001001/123456/999999 rejected by the pre-existing semantic rule, confirmed as an independent layer from the lexical guard), the injectivity sweep (693 distinct instants, zero collisions), timezone equivalence (12:00:00.001Z == 13:00:00.001+01:00 == 07:00:00.001-05:00), distinct-millisecond digest sensitivity, and full parser/constructor equivalence including malformed and naive forms. Discovered a new BLOCKING finding, B-149O.1H.4-1: the 149O.1H.3 lexical guard's regex, _FRACTIONAL_SECONDS_RE = re.compile(r'\.(\d+)(?=Z$|[+-]\d{2}:\d{2}$)'), recognizes only a literal Z suffix or a colon-separated +HH:MM/-HH:MM offset via its lookahead. Python 3.11+'s datetime.fromisoformat is materially more permissive and also accepts non-colon numeric offsets such as +00 (2-digit) and +0000 (4-digit, no colon); for those forms the guard's regex does not match at all (independently confirmed at the regex level: _FRACTIONAL_SECONDS_RE.search('...0000001+00') is None, while the same string with Z or +00:00 does match), so _reject_excess_fractional_precision never raises and the raw issued_at string flows straight into the historically lossy datetime.fromisoformat call unguarded. For the specific 7+-digit values whose truncated (first-6-digit) microsecond value already happens to be millisecond-aligned -- i.e. only the 7th-and-beyond digits are non-zero, such as .0000001 and .0000009 -- this fully bypasses both the lexical guard and the pre-existing millisecond-domain rule (parsed.microsecond % 1000 == 0 for both), reproducing the exact original B-149O.1H-1 collision end-to-end: issued_at='...12:00:00.0000001+00' and issued_at='...12:00:00.0000009+00' both parse and canonicalize to the identical '2026-01-01T12:00:00.000Z', with identical canonical payload bytes for the issued_at field. Independently confirmed via both parse_hatp_proof and the direct HumanApprovalProvenanceProof(...) constructor -- both paths produce the identical (wrong) outcome, so this is a B-149O.1H-1 finding, not a parser/constructor divergence; B-149O.1H-2's shared-validator architecture is confirmed undisturbed (equally exposed on both paths, not divergently exposed). Independently confirmed the bypass is narrow, not wholesale: most 7+-digit non-colon-offset values (e.g. .1234567+05, .1234567-0500, .9999999+00) still truncate to a non-millisecond-aligned microsecond and remain rejected by the pre-existing semantic rule; only the specific all-zero-beyond-sixth-digit subclass fully evades both layers. Independently re-verified B-149O.1H-2's own constructor-hardening regressions (boolean proof_version, invalid repository ID, invalid digests, invalid commit SHA, empty identifier, AG3/AG5 family mismatch): all still correctly rejected -- B-149O.1H-2 REMAINS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED. Independently re-ran closed-schema (13 unknown-field probes), duplicate-key, and AG3/AG5-discrimination regressions: all still correctly rejected -- F-149O.1C-1 INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED IMPLEMENTED (re-evaluated this phase). Independently constructed AG3 and AG5 golden vectors using a canonicalizer written fresh for this phase (not calling or copying canonicalize_hatp_proof_payload) and compared production output byte-for-byte: identical for both families; independently recomputed hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes).hexdigest() and confirmed it matches digest_hatp_proof_payload exactly. Independently verified canonical serializer key-order independence, whitespace independence, and Unicode round-trip; timestamp mutation (.001Z -> .002Z) alters the digest; model immutability holds for both top-level and nested frozen dataclasses; a source-level import/purity/vocabulary audit of the actual code (not docstring prose, which legitimately discusses out-of-scope vocabulary) found no forbidden dependency, no filesystem/network/environment/wall-clock/randomness call, and no VALID/UNKNOWN_SIGNER/approval_present/HATP_VALID symbol in the runtime namespace or document output. Explicitly reconfirmed structural/trust separation: no signature_valid/signer_trusted/human_present/authorized/hatp_valid attribute or document key exists anywhere in the module. New independent verification suite: tests/test_phase_149o_1h_4_hatp_timestamp_canonicalization_final_independent_reverification.py -- 105 tests, all passing, including four tests that reproduce Finding B-149O.1H.4-1 directly (regex-level, parser-level, constructor-level, and scope-boundary confirmation). Files changed: tests/test_phase_149o_1h_4_hatp_timestamp_canonicalization_final_independent_reverification.py (new, 105 tests), docs/PHASE_149O_1H_4_HATP_TIMESTAMP_CANONICALIZATION_FINAL_INDEPENDENT_REVERIFICATION.md (new), PROJECT_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, plus task-lifecycle files. Zero src/pcae/** production files, zero docs/contracts/** files touched -- confirmed via git diff --name-only. Regressions: new suite 105 passed; Wave-3 baseline (test_hatp_proof_models.py + test_hatp_canonical_serialization.py + test_phase_149o_1g_...py 100, test_phase_149o_1h_..._independent_verification.py 166, test_phase_149o_1h_1_..._domain_hardening.py 93, test_phase_149o_1h_2_..._reverification.py 99, test_phase_149o_1h_3_..._repair.py 57) 515 passed, matching the expected count exactly; combined Wave-3 baseline plus this phase's new suite 620 passed; Wave-1/2 foundation (test_repository_identity.py + test_hatp_bootstrap_foundation.py + test_phase_149o_1e_...py + test_phase_149o_1f_...py + test_phase_149o_1f_1_...py) 103 passed; 149O.1F.2 90 passed; phase-report trust (test_phase_reports.py + test_phase_reports_cli.py + test_phase_report_trust_hard_fail.py + test_push_phase_report_identity_137f1.py) 201 passed; HATP contract/plan (test_phase_149o_1c_...py + test_phase_149o_1d_...py) 127 passed, no contract change; RAE/Permission-Broker/agent suite (test_phase_149o_rollback_approval_evidence_canonical_provenance_hardening_independent_verification.py) 4 failed / 13 passed, all 4 confirmed as the same known pre-existing B-149O-1..4-related forgery findings already OPEN, unaffected by this timestamp-only verification phase, zero new failures; Fast Green (-m fast_green -n auto) 4531 passed, identical to the entering baseline, no regression (the new suite is deliberately not registered fast_green, matching this module's existing pattern). Every regression suite matched its expected count exactly; no mismatch findings were generated. B-149O.1H-1 REOPENED -- LOSSY / NON-INJECTIVE TIMESTAMP DOMAIN REMAINS, via Finding B-149O.1H.4-1's non-colon-offset bypass. B-149O.1H-2 REMAINS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED -- PUBLIC CONSTRUCTOR DOMAIN MATCHES STRUCTURAL PARSER DOMAIN. Overall Wave-3 verification verdict: NOT VERIFIED -- BLOCKING HATP WAVE 3 FINDINGS. HATP PRODUCTION: NOT READY (no Wave-4 verifier, no real provider, no Class-B deployment, no RAE integration -- unaffected by, and regardless of, this phase's finding). Recommended next phase: 149O.1H.5 -- narrow repair widening the 149O.1H.3 guard's timezone-suffix coverage (or adopting a suffix-independent fractional-digit-count check), followed by a 149O.1H.6 independent re-verification, before Wave 4/149O.1I may begin. This phase does not implement that repair and does not begin 149O.1I, per its verification-only mandate.
